This sequence ensures replica creation, fault tolerance, application integration, and performance monitoring.

text: Order the steps to configure Amazon CloudFront to serve content from an Amazon S3 bucket.
options: ["Create an Amazon S3 bucket and upload content.","Create a CloudFront distribution, specifying the S3 bucket as the origin.","Configure cache behaviors, security settings (e.g., OAI), and price class.","Update DNS records to point your domain to the CloudFront distribution's domain name."]
explanation: The process begins with preparing the content source, which involves creating an Amazon S3 bucket and uploading the content to be distributed (Option A). text: A solutions architect needs to improve the read performance of an Amazon RDS for MySQL database. Order the steps to implement an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis caching layer.
options: ["Provision an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster.","Modify the application code to first check the cache for data before querying the RDS database.","Configure security groups to allow application access to the ElastiCache cluster.","Monitor cache hit ratio and database load to validate performance improvement."]
explanation: The first step is to provision the Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster (Option A), which will serve as the caching layer. Next, network access must be configured by setting up security groups to allow the application to connect to the ElastiCache cluster (Option C). After the cache is accessible, the application code needs to be modified to implement a caching strategy, typically a 'cache-aside' pattern where the application checks the cache before querying the database (Option B). Finally, monitoring cache hit ratio and database load is crucial to confirm the expected performance improvements (Option D).

text: Order the steps to scale an Amazon RDS for MySQL database using read replicas.
options: ["Create one or more Amazon RDS Read Replicas from the primary database instance.","Modify the application to direct read traffic to the Read Replicas.","Monitor the primary database's CPU utilization and I/O operations.","Verify that read traffic is distributed and primary database load is reduced."]
explanation: To scale read operations, the first step is to create one or more Amazon RDS Read Replicas from the existing primary database instance (Option A). It's important to monitor the primary database's CPU utilization and I/O operations (Option C) to ensure that the read replicas are effectively offloading the read load. Finally, verify that read traffic is indeed distributed and the primary database's load has decreased as expected (Option D).

text: A solutions architect needs to optimize the performance of a data-intensive application using Amazon S3 for large object uploads. Order the steps to implement S3 multipart upload.
options: ["Initiate a multipart upload request to Amazon S3.","Upload object parts in parallel to Amazon S3.","Complete the multipart upload after all parts are uploaded.","Verify the integrity and completeness of the uploaded object."]
explanation: Multipart upload begins by initiating a multipart upload request to Amazon S3, which returns an Upload ID (Option A). With the Upload ID, the object can then be divided into parts, and these parts can be uploaded concurrently (Option B) for improved performance. Once all parts are successfully uploaded, a 'Complete Multipart Upload' request is sent to S3, which reassembles the parts into the final object (Option C). Finally, it's crucial to verify the integrity and completeness of the uploaded object (Option D) to ensure data accuracy.

text: Order the steps to configure Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached for an application.

explanation: The first step is to provision the Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached cluster (Option A). text: A solutions architect wants to optimize compute performance for a batch processing workload. Order the steps to utilize Amazon EC2 Spot Instances effectively.

Once the instances are provisioned, the batch jobs can be processed on them (Option D). Continuous monitoring of Spot Instance interruptions is crucial, and adjustments to the bidding strategy or instance types may be necessary to maintain job completion rates (Option C).

text: Order the steps to configure Amazon CloudFront with an Origin Access Control (OAC) for a private Amazon S3 bucket.
options: ["Create an Amazon S3 bucket and upload content, ensuring it's private.","Create a CloudFront distribution and configure an Origin Access Control (OAC).","Update the S3 bucket policy to grant the OAC permission to access the bucket.","Test access to the S3 content via the CloudFront distribution URL."]
explanation: The first step is to create an Amazon S3 bucket and upload your content, ensuring that the bucket itself is private (Option A). The S3 bucket policy must then be updated to explicitly grant the OAC permission to retrieve objects from the bucket (Option C). text: A solutions architect wants to improve the performance of a web application by using Amazon CloudFront for caching. Order the steps to configure CloudFront for a custom origin (e.g., an EC2 instance or ALB).

text: Order the steps to configure Amazon ElastiCache for Redis with a read replica for improved read scalability.

text: A solutions architect needs to improve the performance of an Amazon DynamoDB table for read-heavy workloads. Order the steps to implement Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX).
options: ["Provision an Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster.","Configure security groups to allow application access to the DAX cluster.","Modify the application code to use the DAX client for DynamoDB operations.","Monitor DAX cache hit ratio and DynamoDB read capacity unit (RCU) consumption."]

text: Order the steps to configure Amazon FSx for Lustre for a high-performance computing (HPC) workload.

text: A solutions architect wants to improve the performance of a web application for global users. Order the steps to implement AWS Global Accelerator.
options: ["Create an AWS Global Accelerator accelerator.","Add one or more listeners to the accelerator to process incoming connections.","Add endpoint groups and endpoints (e.g., Application Load Balancers, EC2 instances) to the listeners.","Update DNS records to point your application's domain name to the Global Accelerator's static IP addresses."]

text: A media company wants to distribute its video content globally with low latency and high transfer speeds. Arrange the following steps in the correct order to configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution for web content delivery.

text: A solutions architect needs to implement a caching layer for a high-traffic web application to improve database performance and reduce latency. Arrange the following steps in the correct order to set up an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster.
options: ["Launch the ElastiCache for Redis cluster, specifying node type, number of shards, and replication groups.","Configure the application to connect to the ElastiCache endpoint for caching operations.","Create a new Amazon VPC Security Group to allow inbound traffic to the ElastiCache cluster from the application's EC2 instances.","Determine the appropriate Redis engine version, node type, and cluster mode (cluster mode enabled or disabled) based on application requirements."]

Option A (Launch the ElastiCache for Redis cluster, specifying node type, number of shards, and replication groups) deploys the caching service. Finally, the application needs to be updated to utilize the new cache. Option B (Configure the application to connect to the ElastiCache endpoint for caching operations) integrates the cache into the application workflow.

text: A database administrator needs to improve the read performance and availability of an Amazon RDS for MySQL database. Arrange the following steps in the correct order to create and utilize an Amazon RDS Read Replica.
options: ["Modify the application to direct read queries to the Read Replica endpoint.","Ensure the source RDS DB instance has automatic backups enabled.","Create a Read Replica from the source RDS DB instance, selecting the desired instance type and Multi-AZ option.","Monitor the Read Replica's performance and replication lag using Amazon CloudWatch."]
explanation: Before creating a Read Replica, the source database must be configured appropriately. Option B (Ensure the source RDS DB instance has automatic backups enabled) is a prerequisite for creating a Read Replica. Once the source is ready, the Read Replica can be provisioned. Option C (Create a Read Replica from the source RDS DB instance, selecting the desired instance type and Multi-AZ option) deploys the read-only copy. To leverage the Read Replica for performance, the application needs to be updated. Option A (Modify the application to direct read queries to the Read Replica endpoint) offloads read traffic. Finally, it's crucial to ensure the Read Replica is functioning as expected. Option D (Monitor the Read Replica's performance and replication lag using Amazon CloudWatch) helps identify any issues and ensures data consistency.

text: A data engineering team needs to upload very large files (e.g., several gigabytes) to Amazon S3 efficiently and reliably. Arrange the following steps in the correct order to perform an S3 multipart upload.
options: ["Upload each part of the file in parallel, specifying the part number.","Initiate a multipart upload request to Amazon S3, receiving an Upload ID.","Combine all uploaded parts into a single object by sending a 'CompleteMultipartUpload' request with the Upload ID and part ETag information.","Divide the large file into smaller, fixed-size parts (e.g., 5 MB or larger)."]
explanation: The first step in a multipart upload is to prepare the data. Option D (Divide the large file into smaller, fixed-size parts (e.g., 5 MB or larger)) breaks the file into manageable chunks. Next, the multipart upload process needs to be formally started with S3. Option B (Initiate a multipart upload request to Amazon S3, receiving an Upload ID) gets a unique identifier for this specific upload. Once initiated, the individual parts can be uploaded. Option A (Upload each part of the file in parallel, specifying the part number) sends the data segments to S3. Finally, after all parts are uploaded, they need to be assembled into the complete object. Option C (Combine all uploaded parts into a single object by sending a 'CompleteMultipartUpload' request with the Upload ID and part ETag information) finalizes the upload.

text: Order the steps to configure an Auto Scaling group for Amazon EC2 instances to ensure application availability and scalability.
options: ["Create an Auto Scaling group, specifying the launch template, desired capacity, and VPC subnets.","Define scaling policies (e.g., target tracking, simple, step scaling) for the Auto Scaling group.","Create an EC2 Launch Template, defining instance type, AMI, security groups, and user data.","Ensure the VPC has subnets configured across multiple Availability Zones for high availability."]
explanation: The foundational step for an Auto Scaling group is to ensure the network infrastructure supports high availability. Option D (Ensure the VPC has subnets configured across multiple Availability Zones for high availability) is crucial. Next, Option C (Create an EC2 Launch Template, defining instance type, AMI, security groups, and user data) specifies how instances will be launched. After the launch template is ready, Option A (Create an Auto Scaling group, specifying the launch template, desired capacity, and VPC subnets) provisions the scaling mechanism. Finally, Option B (Define scaling policies (e.g., target tracking, simple, step scaling) for the Auto Scaling group) configures how the group will dynamically adjust capacity. Creating an Auto Scaling group without a launch template or proper subnets would result in errors or a non-functional scaling solution.

text: Order the steps to set up an Amazon SQS Standard queue for message decoupling between microservices.
options: ["Configure the producing microservice to send messages to the SQS queue.","Create an Amazon SQS Standard queue with appropriate access policies.","Configure the consuming microservice to poll messages from the SQS queue.","Ensure IAM roles for producing and consuming services have SQS permissions."]
explanation: The first step is to provision the messaging service. Option B (Create an Amazon SQS Standard queue with appropriate access policies) establishes the queue. Next, Option D (Ensure IAM roles for producing and consuming services have SQS permissions) provides the necessary authorization for services to interact with the queue. After permissions are set, Option A (Configure the producing microservice to send messages to the SQS queue) integrates the sender. Finally, Option C (Configure the consuming microservice to poll messages from the SQS queue) integrates the receiver, completing the decoupled communication. Attempting to send or receive messages without a queue or proper IAM permissions would result in access denied errors.

text: A solutions architect needs to implement cross-Region failover for a critical database using Amazon RDS Global Database. Order the steps to configure this solution.
options: ["Create a new Amazon RDS Global Database, specifying the primary and secondary AWS Regions.","Promote the secondary Region to primary if a disaster occurs in the original primary Region.","Create a primary database instance within the Global Database in the primary Region.","Create one or more secondary database instances in the secondary AWS Regions."]
explanation: The initial step is to establish the global database structure. Option A (Create a new Amazon RDS Global Database, specifying the primary and secondary AWS Regions) sets up the multi-Region container. Next, Option C (Create a primary database instance within the Global Database in the primary Region) provisions the main operational database. After the primary is ready, Option D (Create one or more secondary database instances in the secondary AWS Regions) establishes the read-only replicas for disaster recovery. Finally, Option B (Promote the secondary Region to primary if a disaster occurs in the original primary Region) is the manual or automated step taken during an actual failover event. Creating instances before the Global Database or attempting promotion without secondary instances would lead to an incomplete or non-functional DR solution.

text: Order the steps to configure an Application Load Balancer (ALB) to distribute traffic to a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances.
options: ["Create a target group and register the EC2 instances as targets.","Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in a VPC with subnets in multiple Availability Zones.","Configure an ALB listener to forward traffic from a specific port/protocol to the target group.","Ensure the EC2 instances' security groups allow inbound traffic from the ALB."]
explanation: The first step is to provision the load balancer itself. Option B (Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in a VPC with subnets in multiple Availability Zones) establishes the core service. Next, Option A (Create a target group and register the EC2 instances as targets) defines where the ALB will send traffic. After the target group is ready, Option C (Configure an ALB listener to forward traffic from a specific port/protocol to the target group) sets up the entry point for traffic. Finally, Option D (Ensure the EC2 instances' security groups allow inbound traffic from the ALB) provides the necessary network access for the ALB to reach the instances. Creating a listener without a target group or without proper security group rules would result in a non-functional load balancer.

text: A solutions architect needs to ensure high availability for a stateful application using Amazon ECS and Amazon EBS. Order the steps to achieve this, considering EBS volume attachment.
options: ["Configure an Amazon ECS service to run tasks in a specific Availability Zone.","Create an Amazon EBS volume in the same Availability Zone as the ECS tasks.","Attach the Amazon EBS volume to the EC2 instance running the ECS task.","Mount the attached EBS volume within the container or EC2 instance operating system."]
explanation: For stateful applications requiring EBS, the EBS volume must be in the same Availability Zone as the compute. Option B (Create an Amazon EBS volume in the same Availability Zone as the ECS tasks) provisions the storage. Next, Option A (Configure an Amazon ECS service to run tasks in a specific Availability Zone) ensures the tasks are launched where the EBS volume is available. After the task is running, Option C (Attach the Amazon EBS volume to the EC2 instance running the ECS task) connects the storage to the compute. Finally, Option D (Mount the attached EBS volume within the container or EC2 instance operating system) makes the data accessible to the application. Attempting to attach an EBS volume across AZs or without a running instance would fail.

text: Order the steps to configure Amazon Route 53 health checks for an application endpoint.
options: ["Associate the health check with a Route 53 DNS record (e.g., failover routing policy).","Define the endpoint to be monitored (e.g., IP address, domain name, path).","Create a Route 53 health check, specifying the protocol, port, and endpoint.","Monitor the health check status and receive notifications if the endpoint becomes unhealthy."]
explanation: The first step is to identify what needs to be monitored. Option B (Define the endpoint to be monitored (e.g., IP address, domain name, path)) specifies the target. Next, Option C (Create a Route 53 health check, specifying the protocol, port, and endpoint) provisions the monitoring mechanism. After the health check is created, Option A (Associate the health check with a Route 53 DNS record (e.g., failover routing policy)) integrates it into DNS routing decisions. Finally, Option D (Monitor the health check status and receive notifications if the endpoint becomes unhealthy) provides operational visibility. Creating a health check without a defined endpoint or associating it with a DNS record before it's ready would be ineffective.

text: A solutions architect needs to proactively handle service quotas for critical AWS services. Order the steps to monitor and manage service quotas using AWS CloudWatch.
options: ["Set up Amazon CloudWatch alarms on the `AWS/Usage` metric namespace for critical service quotas.","Identify the critical AWS service quotas that could impact the application's reliability.","Configure Amazon SNS topics to send notifications when CloudWatch alarms are triggered.","Request a service quota increase through the AWS Service Quotas console if necessary."]
explanation: The initial step is to understand the potential bottlenecks. Option B (Identify the critical AWS service quotas that could impact the application's reliability) focuses on relevant limits. Next, Option A (Set up Amazon CloudWatch alarms on the `AWS/Usage` metric namespace for critical service quotas) establishes proactive monitoring. After alarms are set, Option C (Configure Amazon SNS topics to send notifications when CloudWatch alarms are triggered) ensures that the operations team is alerted. Finally, Option D (Request a service quota increase through the AWS Service Quotas console if necessary) is the action taken when a quota is approaching its limit. Setting up alarms or SNS without identifying critical quotas would lead to unnecessary alerts or missed critical issues.

text: A rapidly growing SaaS application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. During peak usage, the application experiences performance degradation and increased latency due to insufficient compute capacity. The solutions architect needs to implement an automated scaling solution to ensure the application can handle fluctuating demand while maintaining optimal performance and cost efficiency. Arrange the following steps to configure an Auto Scaling group for the EC2 instances.
options: ["Create an Auto Scaling group, specifying the launch template, desired capacity, minimum capacity, and maximum capacity.","Define scaling policies (e.g., target tracking, simple scaling) based on Amazon CloudWatch metrics like CPU utilization or ALB request count per target.","Create an EC2 Launch Template that specifies the instance type, AMI, security groups, and user data for new instances.","Associate the Auto Scaling group with the Application Load Balancer target group to distribute incoming traffic across instances."]
explanation: Configuring an Auto Scaling group for EC2 instances requires a specific order of setup. Option C (Create an EC2 Launch Template that specifies the instance type, AMI, security groups, and user data for new instances) is the prerequisite, as it defines how new instances will be launched. Option A (Create an Auto Scaling group, specifying the launch template, desired capacity, minimum capacity, and maximum capacity) follows, as it uses the launch template to define the scaling boundaries. Option D (Associate the Auto Scaling group with the Application Load Balancer target group to distribute incoming traffic across instances) ensures that newly launched instances are registered with the load balancer. Finally, Option B (Define scaling policies (e.g., target tracking, simple scaling) based on Amazon CloudWatch metrics like CPU utilization or ALB request count per target) enables the automated scaling behavior based on demand. This sequence ensures proper instance definition, scaling group creation, load balancer integration, and dynamic scaling configuration.

text: A healthcare application processes patient data from various sources, requiring high availability and fault tolerance for its database. The solutions architect needs to design a resilient Amazon RDS for MySQL deployment that can withstand an Availability Zone outage and automatically fail over to a healthy instance with minimal data loss. Arrange the following steps to configure a highly available Amazon RDS deployment.
options: ["Configure Amazon CloudWatch alarms to monitor database metrics (e.g., CPU utilization, free storage) and notify operations personnel of potential issues.","Create an Amazon RDS for MySQL instance and select the 'Multi-AZ deployment' option during creation.","Ensure the application connection string uses the RDS endpoint, which automatically resolves to the primary instance, even after a failover.","Regularly test the failover mechanism by initiating a manual failover to verify RTO and RPO objectives are met."]
explanation: To achieve high availability for Amazon RDS, the Multi-AZ deployment is key. Option B (Create an Amazon RDS for MySQL instance and select the 'Multi-AZ deployment' option during creation) is the fundamental step to enable this feature. Option C (Ensure the application connection string uses the RDS endpoint, which automatically resolves to the primary instance, even after a failover) is critical for the application to seamlessly connect to the database regardless of failover. Option A (Configure Amazon CloudWatch alarms to monitor database metrics (e.g., CPU utilization, free storage) and notify operations personnel of potential issues) provides essential monitoring for the database's health. Finally, Option D (Regularly test the failover mechanism by initiating a manual failover to verify RTO and RPO objectives are met) is vital to validate the resilience and recovery capabilities of the setup. This sequence ensures high availability, proper application integration, monitoring, and validation.

text: A large enterprise has several microservices running on Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate. They need to ensure that these services can communicate securely and reliably, even during transient failures or high load. The solutions architect must design a robust inter-service communication strategy that incorporates message queuing and event-driven patterns. Arrange the following steps to implement a message queuing system using Amazon SQS for decoupled microservices.
options: ["Configure the producing microservice to send messages to the Amazon SQS queue.","Create an Amazon SQS queue (Standard or FIFO, depending on ordering requirements) for inter-service communication.","Configure the consuming microservice (e.g., an ECS Fargate task or Lambda function) to poll messages from the SQS queue.","Implement dead-letter queues (DLQs) for the SQS queue to capture messages that fail processing, enabling later analysis and reprocessing."]
explanation: Implementing a message queuing system with Amazon SQS begins with creating the queue itself. Option B (Create an Amazon SQS queue (Standard or FIFO, depending on ordering requirements) for inter-service communication) is the foundational step. Option A (Configure the producing microservice to send messages to the Amazon SQS queue) then enables the first microservice to publish events. Option C (Configure the consuming microservice (e.g., an ECS Fargate task or Lambda function) to poll messages from the SQS queue) allows the second microservice to receive and process these events. Finally, Option D (Implement dead-letter queues (DLQs) for the SQS queue to capture messages that fail processing, enabling later analysis and reprocessing) adds a crucial reliability mechanism for handling failed messages. This sequence ensures queue creation, message production, message consumption, and error handling.

text: A critical backend service processes sensitive customer orders and needs to ensure high reliability. The service uses AWS Lambda functions that are invoked by Amazon SQS. Occasionally, Lambda invocations fail due to transient issues or malformed messages, leading to data loss. The solutions architect needs to implement a robust retry mechanism and error handling for the Lambda function. Arrange the following steps to implement a reliable retry mechanism for a Lambda function processing SQS messages.
options: ["Configure the SQS queue to have a Redrive Policy, specifying a Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) for messages that exceed the maximum receive count.","Configure the AWS Lambda function's error handling to include a retry policy for specific error types and a maximum number of retries.","Set up Amazon CloudWatch alarms to monitor the DLQ's `ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible` metric, alerting operations when messages accumulate.","Ensure the Lambda function code is idempotent, meaning it can safely process the same message multiple times without adverse effects."]
explanation: Implementing a reliable retry mechanism for a Lambda function processing SQS messages starts with ensuring the function's resilience. Option D (Ensure the Lambda function code is idempotent, meaning it can safely process the same message multiple times without adverse effects) is a fundamental best practice for distributed systems and retries. Option B (Configure the AWS Lambda function's error handling to include a retry policy for specific error types and a maximum number of retries) defines how Lambda itself will attempt retries. Option A (Configure the SQS queue to have a Redrive Policy, specifying a Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) for messages that exceed the maximum receive count) then captures messages that fail all retries. Finally, Option C (Set up Amazon CloudWatch alarms to monitor the DLQ's `ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible` metric, alerting operations when messages accumulate) provides crucial visibility into unprocessable messages. This sequence ensures idempotent processing, Lambda-level retries, DLQ for failures, and monitoring.

text: Order the steps to configure an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group to maintain application availability.
options: ["Create an Auto Scaling group, specifying the launch template, desired capacity, and VPC subnets.","Define a launch template (or launch configuration) with the desired EC2 instance type, AMI, and security group.","Attach the Auto Scaling group to an Application Load Balancer target group (optional, but common).","Configure scaling policies (e.g., target tracking, simple scaling) to automatically adjust capacity."]
explanation: Before creating an Auto Scaling group, you need to define how the instances will be launched. Option B describes creating a launch template (or launch configuration) specifying the instance details. Next, the Auto Scaling group itself is created, referencing this launch template and defining its capacity and network placement (Option A). While optional, attaching the Auto Scaling group to an Application Load Balancer target group (Option C) is a common practice for distributing traffic. Finally, scaling policies are configured to automatically adjust the number of instances based on demand (Option D).

text: Order the steps to configure an Application Load Balancer (ALB) to distribute traffic across Amazon EC2 instances.
options: ["Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and configure its listeners.","Register target EC2 instances with the target group.","Create a target group, specifying the protocol and port for health checks.","Update DNS records to point your domain to the ALB's DNS name."]
explanation: The first step is to create the Application Load Balancer (ALB) and configure its listeners to accept incoming traffic on specific ports and protocols (Option A). Next, a target group is created, which defines how the ALB routes requests to registered targets and performs health checks (Option C). The actual EC2 instances (or other targets) are then registered with this target group (Option B). Finally, to direct user traffic to the application, DNS records are updated to point your domain to the ALB's DNS name (Option D).

text: A solutions architect needs to ensure high availability for an Amazon RDS database. Order the steps to configure a Multi-AZ deployment.
options: ["Select the 'Multi-AZ deployment' option during RDS instance creation or modification.","Choose the desired database engine, instance class, and storage type.","Monitor the RDS instance for automatic failover events.","Verify that a synchronous standby replica is provisioned in a different Availability Zone."]
explanation: Configuring Amazon RDS Multi-AZ begins with selecting the core database parameters like engine, instance class, and storage (Option B). The critical step for Multi-AZ is to explicitly select the 'Multi-AZ deployment' option during instance creation or modification (Option A). After this, you should verify that RDS has provisioned a synchronous standby replica in a different Availability Zone (Option D). Finally, it's important to monitor the RDS instance, particularly during maintenance or simulated failures, to observe automatic failover events (Option C).

text: Order the steps to implement a message queue using Amazon SQS and process messages with AWS Lambda.
options: ["Create an Amazon SQS queue.","Configure an AWS Lambda function to process messages.","Set the SQS queue as a trigger for the Lambda function.","Send messages to the SQS queue from a producer application."]
explanation: The first step in setting up a message queue with SQS and Lambda is to create the Amazon SQS queue itself (Option A). Next, the AWS Lambda function that will consume and process these messages needs to be configured (Option B). The crucial link is then established by setting the SQS queue as the trigger for the Lambda function, allowing Lambda to automatically poll and process messages (Option C). Finally, a producer application can begin sending messages to the SQS queue (Option D).

text: A solutions architect needs to implement a highly available and scalable file storage solution. Order the steps to configure Amazon EFS (Elastic File System) for use with Amazon EC2 instances.
options: ["Create an Amazon EFS file system.","Configure EFS mount targets in the desired VPC subnets and security groups.","Mount the EFS file system on Amazon EC2 instances.","Verify that EC2 instances can read and write to the EFS file system."]
explanation: The process begins with creating an Amazon EFS file system (Option A). Next, EFS mount targets must be configured in the appropriate VPC subnets and security groups to allow EC2 instances to connect (Option B). Once mount targets are available, the EFS file system can be mounted on the Amazon EC2 instances (Option C). Finally, it's important to verify that the EC2 instances can successfully read from and write to the EFS file system (Option D).

text: Order the steps to configure Amazon Route 53 health checks for an endpoint.
options: ["Create a Route 53 health check, specifying the endpoint (e.g., IP address, domain name) and monitoring parameters.","Associate the health check with a Route 53 DNS record (e.g., failover, simple routing).","Monitor the health check status in the Route 53 console.","Verify that the DNS record's routing behavior changes based on the health check status."]
explanation: The first step is to create a Route 53 health check, defining the endpoint to monitor and the specific parameters for health evaluation (Option A). Next, this health check is associated with a Route 53 DNS record, enabling Route 53 to use the health status for routing decisions (Option B). It's important to monitor the health check status in the Route 53 console to ensure it's accurately reflecting the endpoint's health (Option C). Finally, verify that the DNS record's routing behavior correctly changes when the health check status changes, for example, during a simulated failure (Option D).

text: A solutions architect wants to implement a highly available caching layer. Order the steps to configure Amazon ElastiCache for Redis in a Multi-AZ setup.
options: ["Provision an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster with replication enabled.","Configure the cluster to have a primary node and one or more read replicas in different Availability Zones.","Update the application to connect to the ElastiCache cluster endpoint.","Monitor the cluster for automatic failover and data replication."]
explanation: The first step is to provision an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster, ensuring that replication is enabled (Option A). Next, configure the cluster to have a primary node and one or more read replicas distributed across different Availability Zones to achieve Multi-AZ high availability (Option B). The application then needs to be updated to connect to the ElastiCache cluster endpoint, which automatically handles routing to the primary node (Option C). Finally, it's crucial to monitor the cluster for automatic failover events and verify data replication between nodes (Option D).

text: Order the steps to configure an Amazon ECS service with AWS Fargate for high availability.
options: ["Create an Amazon ECS cluster.","Define an ECS task definition with your container image and resource requirements.","Create an ECS service, specifying the task definition, desired count, and multiple VPC subnets across AZs.","Attach the ECS service to an Application Load Balancer for traffic distribution."]
explanation: The first step is to create an Amazon ECS cluster, which provides the logical grouping for your services (Option A). Next, you define an ECS task definition, specifying the container image, CPU, memory, and other configurations for your application (Option B). The ECS service is then created, referencing this task definition, setting the desired task count, and crucially, deploying tasks across multiple VPC subnets in different Availability Zones for high availability (Option C). Finally, attaching the ECS service to an Application Load Balancer (Option D) is common practice to distribute incoming traffic across the running tasks.

text: A solutions architect needs to implement a robust event-driven architecture. Order the steps to configure an Amazon SNS topic to publish messages to multiple subscribers.
options: ["Create an Amazon SNS topic.","Create subscriptions to the SNS topic for various endpoints (e.g., SQS queue, Lambda function, email).","Confirm the subscriptions (if required by the endpoint type, like email).","Publish messages to the SNS topic from a publisher application."]
explanation: The first step is to create an Amazon SNS topic, which serves as the central communication channel (Option A). Next, various endpoints that need to receive messages are subscribed to this topic (Option B). For certain subscription types (like email), a confirmation step is required to activate the subscription (Option C). Finally, once the topic and subscriptions are set up, a publisher application can send messages to the SNS topic, which will then be fanned out to all confirmed subscribers (Option D).

text: Order the steps to configure an Amazon S3 bucket for static website hosting with high availability.
options: ["Create an Amazon S3 bucket and upload your static website content.","Enable static website hosting on the S3 bucket and specify an index document.","Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the S3 bucket as its origin.","Update your domain's DNS records to point to the CloudFront distribution."]
explanation: The process begins with creating an Amazon S3 bucket and uploading all static website content to it (Option A). Next, static website hosting is enabled on the S3 bucket, and an index document (e.g., index.html) is specified (Option B). For high availability and performance, an Amazon CloudFront distribution is then configured, using the S3 bucket as its origin (Option C). Finally, to make the website accessible via your custom domain, you update your domain's DNS records to point to the CloudFront distribution's domain name (Option D).

text: A solutions architect needs to design a resilient workflow. Order the steps to implement a serverless workflow using AWS Step Functions.
options: ["Define the state machine using Amazon States Language (JSON).","Create the AWS Step Functions state machine.","Implement the AWS Lambda functions or other services that the state machine will invoke.","Start an execution of the state machine."]
explanation: Before defining the workflow, the individual components (like AWS Lambda functions) that the state machine will invoke need to be implemented (Option C). Once the components are ready, the state machine's logic and flow are defined using Amazon States Language (Option A). After defining the logic, the AWS Step Functions state machine is created based on this definition (Option B). Finally, to run the workflow, an execution of the state machine is started (Option D).

text: Order the steps to configure an Amazon Aurora Global Database for multi-Region disaster recovery.
options: ["Create an Amazon Aurora database cluster in the primary AWS Region.","Add a secondary Aurora cluster in a different AWS Region to the global database.","Configure application endpoints to connect to the primary cluster for writes and secondary for reads (optional).","Monitor replication lag and perform regular disaster recovery drills."]
explanation: The first step is to create an Amazon Aurora database cluster in the primary AWS Region (Option A). To enable multi-Region disaster recovery, a secondary Aurora cluster is then added to the global database in a different AWS Region (Option B). While not strictly required for DR, configuring application endpoints to direct writes to the primary and reads to the secondary can optimize performance (Option C). Finally, continuous monitoring of replication lag and regular disaster recovery drills are crucial to ensure the global database is ready for failover (Option D).

text: A solutions architect needs to ensure a web application running on Amazon EC2 instances can automatically scale to handle varying traffic loads and distribute traffic efficiently. Arrange the following steps in the correct order to set up an Application Load Balancer (ALB) with an Auto Scaling Group (ASG).
options: ["Create an Auto Scaling Group (ASG) and attach it to the target group, specifying desired capacity and scaling policies.","Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and configure listeners for incoming traffic.","Launch an EC2 instance and create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) to serve as the golden image for the ASG.","Create a target group for the ALB and define health checks for the EC2 instances."]
explanation: The first step in setting up an ALB with an ASG is to prepare the compute resource that the ASG will launch. Option C (Launch an EC2 instance and create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) to serve as the golden image for the ASG) provides the template. Next, the load balancer needs to be created to distribute incoming traffic. Option B (Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and configure listeners for incoming traffic) sets up the entry point. After the ALB is ready, it needs a way to route traffic to healthy instances. Option D (Create a target group for the ALB and define health checks for the EC2 instances) defines the backend for the ALB. Finally, the ASG can be created and linked to the target group to manage the EC2 instances. Option A (Create an Auto Scaling Group (ASG) and attach it to the target group, specifying desired capacity and scaling policies) enables automatic scaling and instance management.

text: A microservices architecture requires asynchronous communication between services to improve reliability and decouple components. Arrange the following steps in the correct order to implement a message queue using Amazon SQS and an AWS Lambda consumer.
options: ["Configure the AWS Lambda function as an event source for the SQS queue.","Create an Amazon SQS Standard queue.","Develop and deploy an AWS Lambda function to process messages from the SQS queue.","Configure the producing application to send messages to the SQS queue."]
