options: ["AWS Migration Hub","AWS Application Discovery Service","AWS DMS","AWS Application Migration Service (MGN)","AWS Control Tower"]
explanation: Option A (AWS Migration Hub) provides a single location to track the progress of application migrations across multiple AWS and partner solutions. Option B (AWS Application Discovery Service) helps you identify servers, databases, and other assets in your on-premises data centers, collecting configuration and performance data for migration planning. Option C (AWS DMS) is for database migration. Option D (AWS Application Migration Service (MGN)) is for server rehosting. Option E (AWS Control Tower) is for multi-account governance.

text: When evaluating migration strategies using the 7 Rs, which two approaches involve moving applications to AWS with minimal or no changes to the application architecture? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Rehost","Refactor","Replatform","Retire","Repurchase"]
explanation: Option A (Rehost), also known as 'lift-and-shift,' involves moving applications to AWS without making any changes to the application architecture. Option C (Replatform), also known as 'lift-tinker-and-shift,' involves making a few cloud-native optimizations to realize some benefits without changing the core architecture. Option B (Refactor) involves significant architectural changes to leverage cloud-native features. Option D (Retire) means decommissioning applications. Option E (Repurchase) means moving to a different product, typically SaaS.

text: Which two activities are essential for developing a business case for cloud migration, focusing on financial aspects? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Refactoring applications","Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) analysis","Workload discovery using AWS Application Discovery Service","Identifying cloud-native benefits","Developing a detailed migration plan"]
explanation: Option B (Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) analysis) is crucial for a business case, as it compares the costs of running IT infrastructure on-premises versus in the cloud over a period. Option D (Identifying cloud-native benefits) helps quantify the value proposition beyond just cost savings, such as increased agility, scalability, and innovation, which are key to a strong business case. Option A (Refactoring applications) is a migration strategy, not directly part of business case development. Option C (Workload discovery using AWS Application Discovery Service) is for inventory, which feeds into TCO but isn't the analysis itself. Option E (Developing a detailed migration plan) comes after the business case is approved.

text: Which two AWS services are specifically designed to aid in the discovery of on-premises resources and tracking the migration process to AWS? (Select TWO.)
options: ["AWS DataSync","AWS Application Discovery Service","AWS Migration Hub","AWS DMS","AWS Control Tower"]
explanation: Option B (AWS Application Discovery Service) helps you identify servers, databases, and other assets in your on-premises data centers, collecting configuration and performance data. Option C (AWS Migration Hub) provides a single location to track the progress of application migrations across multiple AWS and partner solutions. Option A (AWS DataSync) is for online data transfer. Option D (AWS DMS) is for database migration. Option E (AWS Control Tower) is for multi-account governance.

text: When planning a migration, which two of the 7 Rs of migration involve changing how an application is run or consumed, rather than just moving it? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Rehost","Refactor","Retire","Repurchase","Relocate"]
explanation: Option B (Refactor/Re-architect) involves fundamentally changing the application's architecture to fully leverage cloud-native capabilities and improve agility, scalability, and performance. Option D (Repurchase) involves moving to a different product, typically a SaaS offering, which changes how the application is consumed. Option A (Rehost) is a lift-and-shift with minimal changes. Option C (Retire) means decommissioning. Option E (Relocate) involves moving hypervisors to EC2 without changing the application, similar to rehost.

text: A company is performing a portfolio assessment to identify migration candidates. Which two outcomes are common goals of this assessment phase? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Developing new application features","Identifying applications suitable for cloud migration","Determining the optimal migration strategy (e.g., Rehost, Refactor)","Implementing a new CI/CD pipeline","Setting up AWS accounts for the entire organization"]
explanation: Option B (Identifying applications suitable for cloud migration) is a primary goal of a portfolio assessment, categorizing which applications are good candidates. Option C (Determining the optimal migration strategy (e.g., Rehost, Refactor)) for each identified application is also a key outcome, aligning the application with one of the 7 Rs. Option A (Developing new application features) is a post-migration activity. Option D (Implementing a new CI/CD pipeline) is part of modernization, often after migration. Option E (Setting up AWS accounts for the entire organization) is part of foundational setup, often preceding detailed migration planning.

text: Which two of the 7 Rs of migration involve eliminating or replacing existing applications or systems? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Rehost","Retire","Replatform","Repurchase","Refactor"]
explanation: Option B (Retire) involves decommissioning applications that are no longer needed, eliminating them from the portfolio. Option D (Repurchase) involves replacing an existing application with a new, typically SaaS-based, product, effectively eliminating the old system. Option A (Rehost), Option C (Replatform), and Option E (Refactor) all involve migrating and continuing to use the application, albeit with different levels of modification.

text: A company is evaluating its on-premises data centers for potential migration to AWS. They need to identify all servers, applications, and network dependencies to build a comprehensive migration plan. Which AWS services can assist with discovering and mapping their on-premises environment? (Select TWO.)
options: ["AWS Application Discovery Service","AWS Migration Hub","AWS DataSync","AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT)","AWS Application Migration Service (MGN)"]
explanation: Option A (AWS Application Discovery Service) is specifically designed to help plan migration projects by identifying on-premises applications, their dependencies, and performance profiles. Option B (AWS Migration Hub) provides a single location to track the progress of migrations across multiple AWS and partner solutions, and it integrates with AWS Application Discovery Service for discovery data. Option C (AWS DataSync) is for online data transfer, not discovery. Option D (AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT)) is for database schema conversion. Option E (AWS Application Migration Service (MGN)) is for rehosting servers, not for initial discovery.

text: When evaluating existing workloads for migration to AWS, a Solutions Architect needs to categorize them based on the '7 Rs of Migration' strategy. Which of the following are valid 'R' strategies? (Select THREE.)
options: ["Rehost","Refactor","Replicate","Relocate","Re-evaluate"]
explanation: Option A (Rehost), Option B (Refactor), and Option D (Relocate) are all valid strategies within the '7 Rs of Migration' framework. Rehost (lift-and-shift) moves applications without changes. Refactor (re-architect) reimagines how an application is architected and developed. Relocate moves hypervisors or entire environments without purchasing new hardware, re-writing applications, or modifying existing operations. Option C (Replicate) is not one of the standard 7 Rs. Option E (Re-evaluate) is a step in the process but not one of the 7 R strategies.

text: A company has several legacy applications running on aging on-premises servers. They want to move these applications to AWS with the LEAST amount of application code change, while still leveraging cloud benefits. Which migration strategies are most suitable for these applications? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Rehost","Refactor","Replatform","Retire","Repurchase"]
explanation: Option A (Rehost), also known as 'lift-and-shift,' involves moving applications to AWS without making any changes to the application architecture, minimizing code changes. Option C (Replatform) involves making some cloud-native optimizations to the application to achieve tangible benefits without changing the core architecture, such as migrating to a managed database service. Option B (Refactor) involves significant code changes to fully leverage cloud-native capabilities, which contradicts the 'least amount of code change' requirement. Option D (Retire) means decommissioning applications, which is not a migration. Option E (Repurchase) involves moving to a different product, typically SaaS, which would involve significant changes from the existing application.

text: Which of the following are valid 'R' strategies within the AWS 7 Rs of Migration framework? (Select THREE.)
options: ["Rehost","Retire","Rebuild","Replatform","Redesign"]
explanation: Option A (Rehost), Option B (Retire), and Option D (Replatform) are all recognized strategies within the AWS 7 Rs of Migration framework. Rehost involves moving applications without changes. Retire means decommissioning applications that are no longer needed. Replatform involves making some cloud-native optimizations without changing the core architecture. Option C (Rebuild) and Option E (Redesign) are not standard terms in the 7 Rs, though 'Refactor' (which is similar to redesign/rebuild) is. The 7 Rs are: Rehost, Replatform, Refactor, Repurchase, Retain, Retire, Relocate.

text: A Solutions Architect is performing a migration readiness assessment for an on-premises environment. Which of the following are key benefits of using AWS Application Discovery Service? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Collects server configuration and performance data","Automates database schema conversion","Maps application dependencies","Performs server rehosting to EC2","Provides a central dashboard for migration tracking"]
explanation: Option A (Collects server configuration and performance data) is a primary function of AWS Application Discovery Service, gathering details like CPU, memory, disk usage, and network information. Option C (Maps application dependencies) is another key benefit, as it helps visualize connections between applications, servers, and databases, which is crucial for migration planning. Option B (Automates database schema conversion) is handled by AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT). Option D (Performs server rehosting to EC2) is the function of AWS Application Migration Service (MGN). Option E (Provides a central dashboard for migration tracking) is the role of AWS Migration Hub.

text: A company is planning to migrate a portfolio of applications to AWS. They want to use AWS Migration Hub to centralize the tracking of their migration progress. Which of the following capabilities does AWS Migration Hub provide? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Provides a single dashboard for tracking migrations","Automates the rehosting of servers to EC2","Integrates with various AWS migration tools","Performs real-time database replication","Discovers on-premises server inventory"]
explanation: Option A (Provides a single dashboard for tracking migrations) is a core feature of AWS Migration Hub, offering a unified view of migration progress across different tools and applications. Option C (Integrates with various AWS migration tools) is also a key capability, allowing Migration Hub to pull data from services like AWS Application Migration Service (MGN), AWS Database Migration Service (DMS), and partner solutions. Option B (Automates the rehosting of servers to EC2) is handled by AWS Application Migration Service (MGN). Option D (Performs real-time database replication) is a function of AWS Database Migration Service (DMS). Option E (Discovers on-premises server inventory) is primarily handled by AWS Application Discovery Service, which can then feed data into Migration Hub.

text: A Solutions Architect is advising a client on migration strategies for their diverse application portfolio. The client wants to minimize operational effort and realize cloud-native benefits where appropriate. Which of the following strategies align with this goal? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Refactor","Repurchase","Rehost all applications to minimize initial effort","Retain all applications on-premises","Relocate virtual machines to VMware Cloud on AWS"]
explanation: Option A (Refactor) involves re-architecting applications to fully leverage cloud-native capabilities, which significantly minimizes operational effort in the long run and maximizes cloud benefits. Option B (Repurchase) involves moving to a SaaS solution, which completely offloads operational overhead to the SaaS provider. Option C (Rehost all applications to minimize initial effort) is an anti-pattern ([ap-4.1-001]) because while it minimizes initial effort, it moves technical debt to the cloud without realizing significant cloud-native benefits or operational efficiency gains. Option D (Retain all applications on-premises) does not involve migration or realizing cloud benefits. Option E (Relocate virtual machines to VMware Cloud on AWS) is a specific type of rehost/relocate that maintains a VMware environment, which might not fully minimize operational effort or realize cloud-native benefits compared to refactoring or repurchasing.

text: A company is migrating its on-premises applications to AWS. They need to identify all running processes, network connections, and resource utilization of their servers to understand their current state and plan for right-sizing in the cloud. Which AWS services can provide this detailed operational data? (Select TWO.)
options: ["AWS Application Discovery Service","AWS Migration Hub","AWS DataSync","AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT)","AWS Application Migration Service (MGN)"]
explanation: Option A (AWS Application Discovery Service) collects detailed configuration and performance data from on-premises servers, including running processes, network connections, and resource utilization, which is essential for right-sizing and migration planning. Option B (AWS Migration Hub) serves as a central hub that aggregates discovery data from AWS Application Discovery Service and other tools, providing a consolidated view of the on-premises environment and tracking migration progress. Option C (AWS DataSync) is for data transfer, not discovery. Option D (AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT)) is for database schema conversion. Option E (AWS Application Migration Service (MGN)) is for rehosting servers, not for initial discovery and data collection.

text: A large enterprise is planning to migrate a critical, monolithic on-premises application with significant technical debt to AWS. The application is business-critical, but its current architecture hinders innovation and scalability. The leadership team wants to embrace cloud-native patterns and improve developer agility, rather than simply rehosting. Which two migration strategies should the solutions architect prioritize to achieve these long-term goals? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Option A: Rehost the application using AWS Application Migration Service (MGN) to quickly move it to Amazon EC2, then optimize later.","Option B: Refactor the application by breaking it into microservices and deploying them on AWS Lambda and Amazon ECS.","Option C: Replatform the application by migrating its components to managed AWS services like Amazon RDS and Amazon ECS Fargate.","Option D: Repurchase a SaaS solution that provides similar functionality to replace the existing application entirely.","Option E: Retain the application on-premises due to the high effort involved in refactoring."]
explanation: Option B (correct) involves refactoring, which means re-architecting the application to take full advantage of cloud-native capabilities, such as microservices on AWS Lambda and Amazon ECS. This directly addresses the goal of embracing cloud-native patterns and improving agility. Option C (correct) suggests replatforming, which involves moving to managed AWS services (like Amazon RDS for databases and Amazon ECS Fargate for containers) to reduce operational overhead and gain cloud benefits without a full re-architecture. Both refactoring and replatforming are suitable for achieving long-term cloud-native benefits and agility. Option A (incorrect) describes rehosting, which is a lift-and-shift approach. While it offers a quick migration, it moves technical debt to the cloud without realizing significant cloud-native benefits, which contradicts the stated goal of embracing cloud-native patterns. This aligns with anti-pattern ap-4.1-001. Option D (incorrect) is repurchase, which might be a valid strategy for some workloads but is not a direct migration strategy for an existing application that the company wants to modernize and operate. Option E (incorrect) suggests retaining the application on-premises, which goes against the objective of migrating to AWS and improving the application's architecture.

text: A global manufacturing company operates hundreds of on-premises servers and virtual machines across various data centers. They need to gain a comprehensive understanding of their server inventory, network dependencies, and application performance profiles to inform their cloud migration strategy. The goal is to automate data collection and centralize visibility into their entire IT estate. Which two AWS services should a Solutions Architect recommend for automated discovery and centralized migration tracking? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Option A: AWS Migration Hub to provide a single dashboard for tracking migration progress across multiple tools.","Option B: AWS Application Discovery Service to automatically collect configuration, performance, and dependency data from on-premises servers.","Option C: AWS Config to monitor and record AWS resource configurations and changes over time.","Option D: AWS Systems Manager to manage and automate operational tasks across EC2 instances and on-premises servers.","Option E: Amazon CloudWatch to collect and track metrics, collect log files, and set alarms for AWS resources."]
explanation: Option A (correct) is AWS Migration Hub, which provides a central location to track the progress of application migrations across multiple AWS and partner solutions. This directly addresses the need for centralized visibility and tracking. Option B (correct) is AWS Application Discovery Service, which helps plan migration projects by automatically identifying applications running in on-premises data centers, their associated dependencies, and performance profiles. This service is crucial for automated data collection and understanding the IT estate. Option C (incorrect) is AWS Config, which is primarily used for monitoring and recording configurations of AWS resources, not for discovering on-premises assets for migration planning. Option D (incorrect) is AWS Systems Manager, which is used for operational management and automation of instances, but not its primary purpose is not on-premises discovery for migration planning. Option E (incorrect) is Amazon CloudWatch, which is a monitoring service for AWS resources and applications, not for on-premises discovery or centralized migration tracking.

text: A Chief Financial Officer (CFO) at a large enterprise is skeptical about the financial benefits of migrating their on-premises data centers to AWS. The solutions architect needs to prepare a compelling argument that goes beyond just infrastructure costs, demonstrating the full economic impact and operational advantages of the cloud. Which two key components should be emphasized when developing a business case and Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) analysis for the migration? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Option A: Focus solely on the direct cost comparison of server hardware and software licenses between on-premises and AWS.","Option B: Include the operational cost savings from reduced data center management, power, cooling, and network infrastructure.","Option C: Quantify the business value derived from increased agility, faster time-to-market, and improved scalability for new initiatives.","Option D: Exclude the cost of new cloud-native skill acquisition and training, assuming existing staff can adapt immediately.","Option E: Present a TCO model that only considers a rehost strategy, as it's the simplest to estimate."]
explanation: Option B (correct) is crucial for a comprehensive TCO analysis. Cloud migration significantly reduces operational costs associated with physical data centers, including power, cooling, physical security, and network infrastructure, as well as the labor involved in managing these. Option C (correct) addresses the business value, which is often a major driver for cloud adoption. Increased agility, faster time-to-market for new products, and the ability to scale rapidly translate into significant competitive advantages and revenue opportunities that must be quantified in a robust business case. Option A (incorrect) is too narrow; focusing solely on direct hardware and software costs overlooks significant operational and business benefits, leading to an incomplete and potentially misleading TCO. Option D (incorrect) is a common oversight. Training and upskilling staff for cloud environments are essential investments and must be included in the TCO analysis to provide a realistic financial picture. Option E (incorrect) aligns with anti-pattern ap-4.1-001. A TCO model should evaluate various migration strategies (rehost, replatform, refactor) to find the optimal path, not default to rehost, especially when seeking broader benefits.

text: A company is conducting a portfolio assessment of its 150 on-premises applications to determine their suitability for cloud migration. Some applications are critical but have strict regulatory compliance requirements tied to specific on-premises hardware, while others are rarely used and have outdated technology. The solutions architect needs to recommend strategies that optimize the migration effort and cost by addressing these diverse application profiles. Which two 7 Rs migration strategies should be applied in this scenario? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Option A: Rehost all applications to Amazon EC2 to achieve the fastest migration timeline.","Option B: Retire applications that are no longer needed or provide minimal business value.","Option C: Retain applications on-premises if they have unique regulatory or technical constraints that make cloud migration impractical or excessively costly.","Option D: Refactor all applications into serverless microservices to maximize cloud-native benefits.","Option E: Repurchase commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) software for all legacy applications."]
explanation: Option B (correct) is the 'Retire' strategy. For applications that are rarely used or provide minimal business value, retiring them eliminates unnecessary migration effort and ongoing costs, optimizing the overall portfolio. Option C (correct) is the 'Retain' strategy. Applications with strict regulatory compliance tied to specific on-premises hardware, or those with prohibitive migration costs, might be best kept on-premises. This acknowledges that not every workload is suitable for immediate cloud migration. Option A (incorrect) is the 'Rehost' strategy for all applications. While quick, it doesn't address the goal of optimizing effort for diverse profiles and can lead to migrating technical debt, especially for outdated or unnecessary applications (anti-pattern ap-4.1-001). Option D (incorrect) is the 'Refactor' strategy for all applications. While beneficial for modernization, refactoring every application is a massive undertaking, potentially impractical for all 150 applications, especially those that are rarely used. Option E (incorrect) is the 'Repurchase' strategy. While valid for some COTS applications, it's not a universal solution for all legacy applications and might not be suitable for custom-built systems.

text: A company's migration team has proposed a 'lift and shift' strategy for all 300 on-premises applications to meet an aggressive 12-month timeline. While this approach offers speed, many of these applications are monolithic, tightly coupled, and have accumulated significant technical debt over years. The business leadership is concerned that this strategy will not fully leverage AWS's capabilities and may hinder future innovation. Which two actions should the solutions architect recommend to address these concerns and align with AWS best practices? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Option A: Proceed with the rehost strategy for all applications to ensure the aggressive timeline is met, deferring modernization efforts.","Option B: Conduct a detailed workload assessment to identify applications that are good candidates for replatforming or refactoring.","Option C: Prioritize refactoring for well-architected applications that would significantly benefit from cloud-native services like AWS Lambda or Amazon ECS.","Option D: Utilize AWS Application Migration Service (MGN) for all migrations, as it is designed for rapid rehosting.","Option E: Focus on migrating only the databases first, leaving the application layer on-premises for a phased approach."]
explanation: Option B (correct) is essential. A detailed workload assessment helps determine the most appropriate 'R' (rehost, replatform, refactor, etc.) for each application, ensuring that the migration strategy aligns with business goals and technical characteristics. This avoids the anti-pattern of defaulting to rehost for all workloads. Option C (correct) emphasizes prioritizing modernization for suitable applications. Well-architected applications, or those with clear benefits from cloud-native patterns, should be refactored or replatformed to realize the full potential of AWS, such as improved scalability, agility, and reduced operational overhead. Option A (incorrect) directly embodies anti-pattern ap-4.1-001, which states that defaulting to rehost for all workloads minimizes migration effort but moves technical debt to the cloud without realizing cloud-native benefits. Option D (incorrect) suggests using AWS Application Migration Service (MGN) for all migrations. While MGN is excellent for rehosting, using it for *all* migrations without considering other strategies like replatforming or refactoring would perpetuate the anti-pattern. Option E (incorrect) proposes migrating only databases first. While a phased approach can be good, this specific phase might not address the core issue of application modernization and could introduce complex hybrid dependencies without a clear overall strategy.

text: A company is planning to migrate its on-premises applications to AWS and needs to gain visibility into its current server inventory, application dependencies, and resource utilization. Which AWS services can assist in collecting this information for migration planning? (Select TWO.)
options: ["AWS Application Discovery Service","AWS DataSync","AWS Migration Hub","AWS Database Migration Service (DMS)","AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT)"]
explanation: Option A (AWS Application Discovery Service) is correct because it helps identify applications running in on-premises data centers, their dependencies, and performance characteristics. Option C (AWS Migration Hub) is correct because it provides a single location to track the progress of application migrations across multiple AWS and partner solutions, and it integrates with AWS Application Discovery Service for discovery. Option B (AWS DataSync) is incorrect as it is used for online data transfer between on-premises storage and AWS storage services, not for application discovery. Option D (AWS Database Migration Service (DMS)) is incorrect as it is specifically for migrating databases. Option E (AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT)) is incorrect as it is used to convert database schemas from one engine to another.

text: When evaluating existing workloads for migration to AWS, a Solutions Architect must consider various strategies, often referred to as the '7 Rs of migration'. Which of the following are valid migration strategies within this framework? (Select THREE.)
options: ["Rehost","Re-evaluate","Replatform","Refactor","Re-architect"]
explanation: Option A (Rehost) is correct. Also known as 'lift and shift', this strategy involves moving applications without making any changes. Option C (Replatform) is correct. This involves making some cloud-native optimizations to achieve a tangible benefit, but without changing the core architecture of the application. Option D (Refactor) is correct. This involves re-imagining how an application is architected and developed, typically using cloud-native features to improve agility, scalability, and performance. Option B (Re-evaluate) is not one of the standard 7 Rs of migration. Option E (Re-architect) is often used interchangeably with Refactor, but 'Refactor' is the more precise term within the 7 Rs framework.

text: Before initiating a large-scale migration, a company needs to centralize its migration planning and track the progress of various migration activities across different tools. They also require a service to discover detailed information about their on-premises server inventory. Which AWS services would fulfill these requirements? (Select TWO.)
options: ["AWS Migration Hub","AWS DMS","AWS Application Discovery Service","AWS Snow Family","AWS DataSync"]
explanation: Option A (AWS Migration Hub) is correct because it provides a single location to track the progress of application migrations across multiple AWS and partner solutions, centralizing planning and tracking. Option C (AWS Application Discovery Service) is correct because it helps collect detailed information about on-premises servers, including inventory, configuration, and performance data, which is crucial for migration planning and populating Migration Hub. Option B (AWS DMS) is incorrect as it is for database migration, not general discovery or centralized tracking of all migration activities. Option D (AWS Snow Family) is incorrect as it is for offline data transfer. Option E (AWS DataSync) is incorrect as it is for online data transfer between on-premises and AWS storage, not for discovery or centralized migration tracking.

text: Order the initial steps a Solutions Architect would take to assess an on-premises environment for potential migration using AWS tools.
options: ["Install AWS Application Discovery Service agents on servers.","Define migration goals and scope.","Analyze collected data for dependencies and utilization.","Integrate collected data with AWS Migration Hub."]
explanation: The first step in any migration assessment is to define the migration goals and scope (Option B). Once goals are set, AWS Application Discovery Service agents can be installed on servers to collect data (Option A). This collected data is then integrated with AWS Migration Hub (Option D) for a centralized view. Finally, the data is analyzed for dependencies and utilization patterns (Option C) to inform migration planning.

text: A company is evaluating its application portfolio for cloud migration. Order the common '7 R' migration strategies from the least to most significant architectural change.
options: ["Replatform (lift-and-tinker)","Rehost (lift-and-shift)","Refactor (re-architect)","Retire (remove)"]
explanation: The '7 R' migration strategies categorize approaches to moving workloads to the cloud. 'Retire' (Option D) involves removing applications that are no longer needed, representing no architectural change. 'Rehost' (Option B), or lift-and-shift, moves applications as-is to AWS, requiring minimal architectural change. 'Replatform' (Option A), or lift-and-tinker, involves making some cloud optimizations without changing the core architecture. 'Refactor' (Option C), or re-architect, involves re-imagining how an application is architected and developed, representing the most significant architectural change.

text: Order the steps to track the progress of a migration project using AWS Migration Hub.
options: ["Group discovered servers into applications.","Import discovered server data into AWS Migration Hub.","Monitor migration status and progress dashboards.","Initiate server migration using integrated migration tools."]
explanation: To track migration progress, the first step is to import discovered server data into AWS Migration Hub (Option B). Once data is imported, you can group discovered servers into logical applications (Option A) for better organization. Next, you initiate the actual server migration using integrated AWS migration tools (Option D), such as AWS Application Migration Service. Finally, you monitor the migration status and progress through the dashboards provided by AWS Migration Hub (Option C).

text: A Solutions Architect is developing a business case for migrating an on-premises application to AWS. Order the key activities for this process.
options: ["Calculate Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) for current and proposed states.","Identify key stakeholders and their requirements.","Present the business case to leadership for approval.","Analyze potential risks and benefits of migration."]
explanation: Developing a business case for cloud migration begins by identifying key stakeholders and their requirements (Option B) to ensure alignment. Next, a comprehensive Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) analysis is performed (Option A) to compare current on-premises costs with projected AWS costs. Subsequently, potential risks and benefits of the migration are thoroughly analyzed (Option D). The final step is to present the well-researched business case to leadership for approval (Option C).

text: Order the steps for using AWS Application Discovery Service to gather data about on-premises servers.
options: ["Install Discovery Agent or use Agentless Collector.","Review collected data in AWS Migration Hub.","Configure data collection parameters.","Identify on-premises servers for discovery."]
explanation: The process of using AWS Application Discovery Service starts by identifying the specific on-premises servers that need to be discovered (Option D). Next, you install the Discovery Agent on those servers or deploy the Agentless Collector (Option A). After installation, you configure the data collection parameters (Option C), such as what type of data to collect. Finally, the collected data is reviewed within AWS Migration Hub (Option B) to gain insights into the environment.

text: When evaluating an on-premises legacy application for migration, a Solutions Architect must decide between 'rehost' and 'replatform'. Order the considerations for this decision.
options: ["Evaluate the application's compatibility with cloud-native services.","Assess the effort and cost of refactoring the application.","Determine the immediate need for cloud benefits versus migration speed.","Identify existing technical debt and its impact on modernization."]
explanation: When choosing between rehost and replatform, the first consideration is to determine the immediate need for cloud benefits versus migration speed (Option C); rehosting is faster, replatforming offers more benefits. Next, evaluate the application's compatibility with cloud-native services (Option A) to see if replatforming is viable. Then, identify existing technical debt (Option D) that might hinder modernization efforts. Finally, assess the effort and cost of refactoring (Option B), which is a more extensive change than replatforming, to understand the full spectrum of modernization options.

text: A company is initiating its cloud migration journey. Order the typical high-level phases involved in a comprehensive migration project.
options: ["Migrate applications and data","Assess current environment and define strategy","Modernize and optimize workloads","Mobilize and plan the migration"]
explanation: The typical phases of a cloud migration journey begin with assessing the current environment and defining a strategy (Option B). This is followed by a mobilization and planning phase (Option D) to prepare for the migration. Next, the actual migration of applications and data occurs (Option A). Finally, after migration, workloads are modernized and optimized in the cloud (Option C).

text: Order the steps to perform a discovery of on-premises servers and their dependencies using AWS Application Discovery Service.
options: ["Install the AWS Agentless Discovery Connector or Agent on servers","Review discovered data in AWS Migration Hub","Configure data collection in AWS Application Discovery Service","Create an AWS Migration Hub home Region"]
explanation: To perform discovery, you first need to create an AWS Migration Hub home Region (Option D), as Application Discovery Service integrates with Migration Hub. Next, configure data collection within AWS Application Discovery Service (Option C). Then, install the AWS Agentless Discovery Connector or Agent on the on-premises servers (Option A) to collect data. Finally, review the collected and discovered data in AWS Migration Hub (Option B).

text: Order the steps to track the progress of a server migration project using AWS Migration Hub.
options: ["Monitor migration status and progress","Configure data sources for migration tools","Set up a Migration Hub home Region","Group applications and define migration waves"]
explanation: To track migration progress, you must first set up a Migration Hub home Region (Option C). Then, configure data sources for the various migration tools being used (Option B), such as AWS Application Migration Service or AWS Database Migration Service. After data sources are set, group applications and define migration waves (Option D) to organize the migration. Finally, monitor the migration status and progress (Option A) through the Migration Hub dashboard.

text: A company is evaluating its application portfolio for cloud migration. Order the initial steps to apply the 7 Rs of migration framework.
options: ["Categorize applications based on business value and technical complexity","Identify applications suitable for rehosting (lift and shift)","Inventory all on-premises applications and infrastructure","Determine applications to retain or retire"]
explanation: The initial step in applying the 7 Rs framework is to inventory all on-premises applications and infrastructure (Option C) to understand the current state. Next, categorize applications based on their business value and technical complexity (Option A) to inform strategic decisions. Based on this, determine which applications to retain or retire (Option D) as they may not be suitable for migration. Finally, identify applications suitable for rehosting (lift and shift) (Option B), which is often the quickest migration path for compatible workloads.

text: Order the common sequence of activities when developing a Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) analysis for cloud migration.
options: ["Calculate on-premises infrastructure and operational costs","Compare total costs and present findings","Estimate AWS cloud service costs","Identify scope and gather data for analysis"]
explanation: Developing a TCO analysis begins by identifying the scope and gathering relevant data for the analysis (Option D). Next, calculate the current on-premises infrastructure and operational costs (Option A). Then, estimate the corresponding AWS cloud service costs (Option C) for the proposed migration. Finally, compare the total costs (on-premises vs. AWS) and present the findings (Option B) to stakeholders.

text: Order the high-level steps to register a discovered on-premises server with AWS Migration Hub.
options: ["Select the discovered server in AWS Migration Hub","Initiate discovery using AWS Application Discovery Service","Assign the server to an application","Choose a migration tool for the server"]
explanation: The process begins by initiating discovery using AWS Application Discovery Service (Option B) to find on-premises servers. Once discovered, select the specific server in AWS Migration Hub (Option A) to manage it. Then, choose a migration tool for the server (Option D), such as AWS Application Migration Service (MGN), to define how it will be moved. Finally, assign the server to an application (Option C) within Migration Hub for organized tracking.

text: A large enterprise with over 500 on-premises servers and diverse applications plans a significant migration to AWS. The leadership team requires a structured approach to identify, assess, and prioritize workloads, focusing on total cost of ownership (TCO) and aligning with the 7 Rs of migration. The solutions architect needs to establish a clear sequence of initial assessment activities using AWS tools to ensure a data-driven decision-making process. Order the following steps for an initial migration assessment.
options: ["Develop a detailed business case and TCO analysis for identified migration candidates.","Utilize AWS Application Discovery Service to perform automated discovery of on-premises servers and dependencies.","Categorize workloads based on the 7 Rs of migration (rehost, replatform, refactor, etc.) and assess their cloud readiness.","Integrate discovery data into AWS Migration Hub to centralize inventory and track initial assessment progress."]
explanation: The correct sequence for an initial migration assessment starts with discovery. Option B (correct) involves using AWS Application Discovery Service to gather comprehensive data on the existing on-premises environment, which is foundational. Option D (correct) then integrates this discovery data into AWS Migration Hub, providing a centralized view and tracking mechanism. Following discovery, Option C (correct) involves categorizing workloads using the 7 Rs framework and assessing their readiness, which requires the inventory data. Finally, Option A (correct) develops a detailed business case and TCO analysis, which relies on the previous steps of discovery, inventory, and strategy categorization to provide accurate financial projections. Incorrect orderings would lead to incomplete data or premature decision-making.

text: A company is evaluating moving its critical financial reporting system from on-premises to AWS. The Chief Financial Officer (CFO) requires a robust business case that clearly justifies the migration, outlines potential cost savings, and addresses risks. The solutions architect must define a systematic process for developing this business case, ensuring all necessary data points are captured and analyzed before presenting to stakeholders. Order the following steps to develop a comprehensive business case for cloud migration.
options: ["Present the complete business case, including TCO, ROI, and risk mitigation strategies, to executive stakeholders for approval.","Gather comprehensive data on current on-premises infrastructure costs, operational expenses, and application performance metrics.","Perform a Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) analysis, comparing current state costs with estimated AWS costs over a multi-year period.","Identify and assess potential risks associated with the migration and develop mitigation strategies."]
explanation: The logical first step in developing a business case is to collect foundational data. Option B (correct) focuses on gathering current on-premises costs and performance metrics, which are essential inputs. Once this data is available, Option C (correct) performs a TCO analysis, comparing the current state with estimated AWS costs, providing the core financial justification. Following the financial analysis, Option D (correct) identifies and assesses migration risks and outlines mitigation strategies, addressing potential concerns. Finally, Option A (correct) involves presenting the complete business case to stakeholders, which should only occur after all data has been collected, analyzed, and risks addressed. Incorrect orderings would result in a poorly supported or incomplete business case.

text: An organization has initiated a large-scale migration project to AWS, involving hundreds of applications and servers. The migration team needs a centralized way to track the progress of individual application migrations, monitor server replication status, and manage the overall migration workflow. The solutions architect is tasked with configuring AWS Migration Hub to provide this visibility and control. Order the following steps to effectively utilize AWS Migration Hub for tracking a migration project.
options: ["Group discovered servers into applications within AWS Migration Hub and assign migration strategies.","Configure data sources, such as AWS Application Discovery Service or third-party tools, to import server inventory into Migration Hub.","Monitor the migration progress of individual servers and applications through the Migration Hub dashboard.","Initiate server replication or migration tasks using integrated services like AWS Application Migration Service (MGN)."]
explanation: To effectively use AWS Migration Hub, the initial step is to populate it with data. Option B (correct) describes configuring data sources to import server inventory, which is the prerequisite. Once inventory is in Migration Hub, Option A (correct) allows for grouping servers into logical applications and assigning migration strategies, providing structure to the project. After applications are defined, Option D (correct) involves initiating the actual migration tasks using integrated services like MGN. Finally, Option C (correct) is to monitor the ongoing migration progress through the Migration Hub dashboard, which leverages all the previously configured data and tasks. Incorrect sequences would prevent proper data ingestion or logical organization.

text: An IT department is reviewing its portfolio of 100 on-premises applications to determine the most suitable migration strategy for each, aiming to maximize cloud benefits while managing effort. The solutions architect needs to implement a structured approach to apply the 7 Rs of migration (Retain, Retire, Rehost, Replatform, Repurchase, Refactor, Relocate) consistently across the entire portfolio. Order the following steps to systematically apply the 7 Rs of migration to an application portfolio.
options: ["Conduct a detailed technical and business assessment for each application to understand dependencies and requirements.","Categorize each application into one of the 7 Rs based on the assessment, business value, and cloud readiness.","Develop a high-level migration plan for each application, outlining the chosen 7R strategy and initial resource estimates.","Compile a comprehensive inventory of all on-premises applications, including their current state and ownership."]
explanation: The process of applying the 7 Rs starts with understanding the current landscape. Option D (correct) involves compiling a comprehensive inventory of all applications, which is the foundational data collection step. Following this, Option A (correct) conducts a detailed technical and business assessment for each application, providing the necessary depth to make informed decisions. With the assessment complete, Option B (correct) categorizes each application into one of the 7 Rs, which is the core decision-making phase. Finally, Option C (correct) develops a high-level migration plan for each application based on the chosen strategy. Incorrect ordering would lead to decisions without sufficient data or a lack of a structured approach.

text: A legacy monolithic Java application is incurring high operational costs and is difficult to update. The development team is considering modernizing it by refactoring into microservices or simply rehosting it on AWS. The solutions architect needs to guide the team through a structured evaluation process to determine the most beneficial approach, considering both short-term effort and long-term gains. Order the following steps to evaluate an application for refactoring versus rehosting.
options: ["Perform a detailed cost-benefit analysis comparing the long-term operational savings and agility benefits of refactoring against the lower initial effort of rehosting.","Conduct a thorough performance analysis of the current application to identify bottlenecks and areas for improvement.","Map out all application dependencies, including databases, external services, and inter-component communication.","Develop a pilot project or proof-of-concept for the chosen strategy (refactor or rehost) to validate assumptions and gather real-world data."]
explanation: Evaluating refactoring versus rehosting starts with understanding the current state. Option B (correct) involves conducting a thorough performance analysis to identify existing bottlenecks. Concurrently or subsequently, Option C (correct) maps out all application dependencies, which is crucial for understanding the complexity of both rehosting and refactoring. With this understanding, Option A (correct) performs a detailed cost-benefit analysis, comparing the two strategies based on effort, cost, and long-term benefits. Finally, Option D (correct) develops a pilot project for the chosen strategy to validate the approach with real-world data before a full-scale commitment. An incorrect order might lead to making decisions without sufficient data or validating the chosen path.

text: A migration team proposes a blanket 'lift-and-shift' (rehost) strategy for all 200 on-premises applications to minimize initial migration effort. A senior solutions architect is concerned that this approach might move technical debt to the cloud and miss opportunities for modernization. The architect needs to establish a process to challenge this anti-pattern and ensure that each workload's optimal migration strategy is considered. Order the following steps to identify and address anti-patterns in migration planning.
options: ["Assess each workload's characteristics, including its architecture, dependencies, and business criticality, to identify cloud-native benefits that would be missed by simple rehosting.","Review the proposed blanket rehost strategy and identify specific applications that are well-suited for rehosting versus those that would benefit more from replatforming or refactoring.","Propose alternative migration strategies (replatform, refactor, repurchase) for specific workloads, highlighting the long-term operational and cost benefits.","Educate the migration team on the '7 Rs of migration' and the importance of evaluating each workload individually to avoid moving technical debt to the cloud."]
explanation: To address an anti-pattern like defaulting to rehost, the first step is often educational and foundational. Option D (correct) involves educating the team on the 7 Rs, setting the stage for a more nuanced approach. Following this, Option A (correct) assesses individual workload characteristics to identify specific opportunities for cloud-native benefits that a simple rehost would miss. With this assessment, Option B (correct) reviews the proposed blanket strategy against the individual workload characteristics, identifying where rehosting is suboptimal. Finally, Option C (correct) proposes alternative strategies for those specific workloads, backed by the analysis, to achieve better long-term outcomes. An incorrect order would mean challenging the strategy without a clear framework or data.

text: The finance team at a manufacturing company needs to justify a cloud migration by comparing the current on-premises infrastructure costs with the projected costs of running workloads on AWS. The solutions architect is tasked with providing the initial data points required for a comprehensive Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) analysis. Order the following steps for initial data collection for a TCO analysis.
options: ["Estimate the costs of equivalent AWS services (compute, storage, networking, databases) for the identified workloads.","Gather detailed information on current on-premises hardware, software licenses, power, cooling, and data center facility costs.","Factor in potential operational changes, such as reduced administrative overhead or new skill requirements, and their associated costs or savings.","Calculate the initial TCO comparison, highlighting potential savings or increased costs over a specified period."]
explanation: The first step in any TCO analysis is to understand the current state. Option B (correct) focuses on gathering detailed current on-premises costs, which serves as the baseline. Once the current costs are understood, Option A (correct) estimates the costs of running equivalent workloads on AWS, providing the comparison point. Following this, Option C (correct) factors in operational changes, which are crucial for a realistic TCO. Finally, Option D (correct) calculates the initial TCO comparison, which is the culmination of the data collection and estimation. An incorrect order would lead to an inaccurate or incomplete TCO analysis.

text: A solutions architect is evaluating a company's on-premises application portfolio for potential migration to AWS. Order the following stages of the 7 Rs of migration strategy evaluation in a typical logical sequence.
options: ["Rehost (lift and shift) applications with minimal changes.","Refactor (re-architect) applications to leverage cloud-native features.","Retire applications that are no longer needed.","Retain applications that are not suitable for migration at this time."]
explanation: The most logical sequence for evaluating the 7 Rs of migration often starts with identifying applications that can be retired (Option C) or retained (Option D) as they require no migration effort. After this, applications are typically considered for rehosting (Option A) for a quick move to the cloud, followed by refactoring (Option B) to gain cloud-native benefits, which is a more complex and time-consuming process.

text: A company wants to discover its on-premises server inventory and dependencies using AWS Application Discovery Service. Order the steps to achieve this.
options: ["Install the AWS Agentless Collector or Agent-based Collector on-premises.","View discovered server information and dependencies in AWS Migration Hub.","Configure data collection and specify discovery parameters.","Generate reports for migration planning and TCO analysis."]
explanation: The process begins by installing the appropriate collector (Option A) on the on-premises environment to gather data. Next, the data collection parameters need to be configured (Option C). Once data is collected, it can be viewed and analyzed within AWS Migration Hub (Option B). Finally, reports can be generated (Option D) to aid in migration planning and cost analysis.

text: An organization is performing a Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) analysis to justify migrating its on-premises workloads to AWS. Order the following steps for conducting a TCO analysis.
options: ["Estimate the costs of running the workloads on AWS, including compute, storage, and networking.","Identify and quantify all current on-premises costs, such as hardware, software licenses, power, and administration.","Compare the on-premises costs with the estimated AWS costs over a defined period.","Present the TCO analysis findings to stakeholders for decision-making."]
explanation: A TCO analysis starts by understanding the current state, which involves identifying and quantifying all existing on-premises costs (Option B). Then, the estimated costs of running the workloads on AWS are calculated (Option A). These two sets of costs are then compared (Option C) to determine the financial benefits or implications of migration. Finally, the findings are presented to stakeholders (Option D) to inform strategic decisions.

text: A solutions architect is using AWS Migration Hub to track the progress of a large-scale migration project. Order the general steps involved in setting up and utilizing AWS Migration Hub for workload tracking.
options: ["Group discovered servers into applications within Migration Hub.","Initiate data collection from on-premises environments using Application Discovery Service.","Monitor migration progress and status updates for each application.","Configure the Migration Hub home region and connect discovery tools."]
explanation: The initial step is to configure the AWS Migration Hub home region and connect it with discovery tools like AWS Application Discovery Service (Option D). Once connected, data collection from on-premises environments is initiated (Option B). After discovery, servers are grouped into logical applications (Option A) to manage them effectively. Finally, the migration progress for these applications can be monitored (Option C) within Migration Hub.

text: A company is planning a phased migration of its applications to AWS. Order the following conceptual steps for prioritizing workloads in a migration wave.
options: ["Evaluate the business impact and criticality of each application.","Identify interdependencies between applications to minimize disruption.","Assess the technical complexity and effort required for migrating each application.","Sequence applications into migration waves based on risk and benefit."]
explanation: Prioritizing workloads typically begins with assessing the technical complexity and effort (Option C) to understand the migration challenge. Concurrently, the business impact and criticality (Option A) are evaluated to determine the value of migration. Identifying interdependencies (Option B) is crucial to ensure a smooth transition and avoid breaking connections. Finally, applications are sequenced into migration waves (Option D) considering all these factors to manage risk and maximize benefit.

text: A solutions architect is preparing for the migration planning phase of an enterprise cloud adoption journey. Order the following high-level activities in a typical migration planning sequence.
options: ["Define the overall migration strategy and target architecture for key workloads.","Develop a detailed migration runbook with step-by-step procedures.","Assemble and train the dedicated cloud migration team.","Establish security, compliance, and governance frameworks for the cloud environment."]
explanation: The planning phase typically starts with defining the overall migration strategy and target architecture (Option A) to set the direction. Next, assembling and training the migration team (Option C) ensures the right skills are in place. Establishing security, compliance, and governance frameworks (Option D) is critical before any actual migration. Finally, a detailed migration runbook (Option B) is developed to guide the execution.

text: When evaluating a legacy on-premises application for modernization or migration, a solutions architect follows a structured approach. Order these general steps for evaluating a legacy application.
options: ["Identify the current pain points and limitations of the application.","Document the application's current architecture, dependencies, and operational processes.","Select the most suitable migration or modernization strategy (e.g., rehost, refactor).","Explore potential cloud-native alternatives and services that could enhance the application."]
explanation: The evaluation process should begin by thoroughly documenting the application's current state (Option B) to establish a baseline. Following this, identifying current pain points and limitations (Option A) helps pinpoint areas for improvement. Next, exploring cloud-native alternatives (Option D) allows for considering modernization opportunities. Finally, based on the analysis, the most suitable migration or modernization strategy (Option C) is selected.

text: Order the core steps to prepare for a rehost migration using AWS Application Migration Service (MGN).
options: ["Install the AWS Replication Agent on source servers","Configure replication settings in MGN","Add source servers to MGN","Launch test instances to validate replication"]
explanation: To prepare for a rehost migration with MGN, you first add the source servers to MGN (Option C) in the AWS console. Next, configure the replication settings (Option B), such as subnet and security groups. Then, install the AWS Replication Agent on the source servers (Option A) to begin data replication. Finally, launch test instances (Option D) from the replicated data to validate the setup before cutover.

text: Order the steps to configure an AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) replication instance and endpoints for a migration.
options: ["Create a source endpoint for the on-premises database","Create a replication instance in DMS","Create a target endpoint for the AWS database","Create and start a migration task"]
explanation: The initial step is to create a replication instance in DMS (Option B), which performs the actual data migration. Next, create a source endpoint for the on-premises database (Option A), providing connection details. Then, create a target endpoint for the AWS database (Option C), specifying the destination. Finally, create and start a migration task (Option D) to define what data to migrate and begin the process.

text: Order the steps to perform an offline data transfer of large datasets using AWS Snowball Edge.
options: ["Ship the Snowball Edge device back to AWS","Create a job in the AWS Snow Family console","Transfer data from your on-premises storage to the Snowball Edge device","Receive the Snowball Edge device"]
explanation: The process begins by creating a job in the AWS Snow Family console (Option B), specifying the data to be transferred. After the device is prepared, you receive the Snowball Edge device (Option D) at your location. Then, transfer data from your on-premises storage to the Snowball Edge device (Option C). Finally, ship the Snowball Edge device back to AWS (Option A) for data import into Amazon S3.

text: A company plans to migrate a legacy SQL Server database to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. Order the high-level process using AWS migration tools.
options: ["Perform schema conversion and code transformation using AWS SCT","Set up AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) for data replication","Assess the source database for migration complexity","Cut over to the Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL instance"]
explanation: For a heterogeneous database migration, first assess the source database for migration complexity (Option C), often using AWS SCT's assessment report. Next, perform schema conversion and code transformation using AWS SCT (Option A) to convert SQL Server objects to PostgreSQL. Then, set up AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) for data replication (Option B) to move the actual data. Finally, cut over to the Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL instance (Option D) once replication is complete and validated.

text: Order the steps to assess a database for heterogeneous migration compatibility using AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT).
options: ["Connect SCT to the source and target databases","Generate a database migration assessment report","Create a new AWS SCT project","Review the assessment report for conversion complexity"]
explanation: To assess a database with SCT, first create a new AWS SCT project (Option C). Next, connect SCT to both the source and target databases (Option A) to establish communication. Then, generate a database migration assessment report (Option B), which analyzes the compatibility. Finally, review the assessment report for conversion complexity (Option D) and identify any manual conversion efforts required.

text: A remote branch office with limited network connectivity needs to transfer a large amount of backup data to AWS. Order the steps for using AWS DataSync.
options: ["Configure a DataSync task with the source and destination locations","Deploy and activate an AWS DataSync agent in the remote office","Create an Amazon S3 bucket as the destination","Start the DataSync task and monitor progress"]
explanation: First, deploy and activate an AWS DataSync agent in the remote office (Option B) to facilitate secure data transfer from the local storage. Next, create an Amazon S3 bucket (Option C) in AWS to serve as the destination for the backup data. Then, configure a DataSync task (Option A), specifying the on-premises location (via the agent) and the S3 bucket. Finally, start the DataSync task and monitor its progress (Option D) to ensure successful data transfer.

text: A company needs to migrate 50 Windows servers from its on-premises data center to AWS with minimal downtime, as these servers host critical business applications. The solutions architect has chosen AWS Application Migration Service (MGN) for its automated, block-level replication capabilities. The architect must outline the precise sequence of steps to execute this rehost migration efficiently. Order the following steps for a rehost migration using AWS Application Migration Service (MGN).
options: ["Launch test instances on AWS from the replicated data to validate application functionality and performance.","Install the AWS Replication Agent on each source Windows server to initiate block-level data replication to a staging area in AWS.","Configure the replication settings for each source server within the AWS MGN console, specifying target instance types and subnet.","Perform a cutover to the newly launched AWS instances during a planned maintenance window, redirecting traffic to the cloud environment."]
explanation: The migration process with AWS MGN begins with setting up replication. Option B (correct) involves installing the AWS Replication Agent on source servers, which starts the data replication. Following this, Option C (correct) configures the replication settings in the MGN console, defining how the instances will be provisioned in AWS. Once replication is stable, Option A (correct) launches test instances to validate the migrated applications without impacting production. Finally, Option D (correct) performs the cutover during a maintenance window, switching production traffic to the AWS instances. Incorrect ordering would lead to replication issues, unvalidated migrations, or unplanned downtime.

text: A development team needs to migrate a production MySQL database to Amazon RDS for MySQL with minimal downtime, as the application relying on it is critical. The solutions architect has decided to use AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) for an online, continuous replication migration. A precise sequence of configuration and execution steps is required to ensure data integrity and a smooth transition. Order the following steps for an online database migration using AWS DMS.
options: ["Create a DMS replication instance in AWS to perform the data migration.","Configure source and target endpoints in DMS, specifying connection details for the on-premises MySQL database and the Amazon RDS instance.","Create and start a DMS migration task, selecting full load plus change data capture (CDC) for continuous replication.","Monitor the replication task, validate data consistency, and plan a cutover window to switch application traffic to the Amazon RDS instance."]
explanation: The first step in an AWS DMS migration is to provision the necessary infrastructure. Option A (correct) involves creating a DMS replication instance, which is the compute resource for the migration. Next, Option B (correct) configures the source and target endpoints, defining where DMS will read from and write to. After endpoints are set up, Option C (correct) creates and starts the DMS migration task, initiating the data transfer and continuous replication. Finally, Option D (correct) monitors the task and plans the cutover, ensuring data consistency before switching applications. Incorrect ordering would prevent DMS from connecting to databases or initiating replication properly.

text: A company is migrating a legacy Oracle database to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL to leverage open-source benefits and reduce licensing costs. The existing schema and stored procedures are highly customized for Oracle, requiring significant conversion effort. The solutions architect has chosen AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT) to automate much of this process. A clear sequence of operations is needed to ensure a successful schema and code conversion. Order the following steps for schema conversion using AWS SCT.
options: ["Connect AWS SCT to both the source Oracle database and the target Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL instance.","Install and configure AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT) on a client machine or EC2 instance.","Analyze the source schema to identify conversion complexities and generate a database migration assessment report.","Convert the schema and database code (e.g., stored procedures, functions) within SCT and apply it to the target Aurora PostgreSQL database."]
explanation: The process begins with setting up the tool itself. Option B (correct) involves installing and configuring AWS SCT. Once SCT is ready, Option A (correct) connects it to both the source and target databases, establishing communication. After connections are made, Option C (correct) analyzes the source schema, providing insights into conversion complexity. Finally, Option D (correct) converts the schema and applies it to the target database, completing the core task. Incorrect ordering would mean SCT cannot connect to databases or perform analysis.

text: A research institution needs to migrate 500 TB of archival scientific data from a remote on-premises facility with extremely limited internet connectivity to Amazon S3. The data transfer must be secure and efficient, and traditional online methods are not feasible due to bandwidth constraints. The solutions architect has identified AWS Snowball Edge as the optimal solution. Order the following steps for a large-scale offline data migration using AWS Snowball Edge.
options: ["Connect the AWS Snowball Edge device to the on-premises network and transfer the 500 TB of data from local storage to the device.","Order an AWS Snowball Edge device through the AWS Management Console, specifying the desired capacity and S3 bucket for data import.","Ship the filled Snowball Edge device back to AWS.","Monitor the data import process as AWS uploads the data from the device to the designated Amazon S3 bucket."]
explanation: The process starts with requesting the device. Option B (correct) involves ordering an AWS Snowball Edge device through the console. Once the device arrives, Option A (correct) connects it to the local network and transfers the data onto it. After data transfer is complete, Option C (correct) ships the device back to AWS. Finally, Option D (correct) monitors the data import as AWS transfers the data from the device to Amazon S3. Incorrect ordering would mean the device isn't ordered, data isn't transferred, or the device isn't returned for import.

text: A media company needs to migrate 100 TB of NFS share data, including video assets and associated metadata, from its on-premises storage to Amazon S3. The migration must preserve file metadata and be performed securely and efficiently over the network. The solutions architect has selected AWS DataSync for this task due to its ability to handle large transfers and maintain data integrity. Order the following steps for migrating file data from on-premises to Amazon S3 using AWS DataSync.
options: ["Deploy an AWS DataSync agent on-premises in a virtual machine or EC2 instance.","Create a DataSync task, specifying the source NFS location and the target Amazon S3 bucket.","Configure the source location (NFS share) and the destination location (Amazon S3 bucket) within DataSync.","Execute the DataSync task and monitor its progress through the AWS Management Console."]
explanation: The first step for AWS DataSync is to establish connectivity to the on-premises environment. Option A (correct) involves deploying an AWS DataSync agent on-premises. Once the agent is deployed, Option C (correct) configures both the source NFS location and the target Amazon S3 location within DataSync. With locations defined, Option B (correct) creates the DataSync task, linking the source and destination. Finally, Option D (correct) executes the task and monitors its progress. Incorrect ordering would prevent the agent from being available or the locations from being defined before creating the task.

text: A critical production database migration is planned from on-premises SQL Server to Amazon RDS for SQL Server. The solutions architect is acutely aware of the risks associated with database migrations, especially data integrity, and needs to ensure a robust fallback plan is in place to mitigate potential issues during cutover, as per anti-pattern ap-4.2-001. Order the following steps for a database migration with a comprehensive fallback plan.
options: ["Perform a full data validation between the source and target databases in parallel with ongoing replication.","Set up continuous data replication from the on-premises source database to the Amazon RDS target using AWS DMS.","Plan a detailed cutover window, including a tested rollback procedure to revert to the source database if issues arise.","Execute the cutover during the planned window, switching application traffic to the Amazon RDS instance, and perform final validation."]
explanation: To ensure a safe database migration with a fallback, the process begins with establishing replication. Option B (correct) sets up continuous data replication using AWS DMS, ensuring the target database is kept up-to-date. Concurrently with replication, Option A (correct) performs full data validation to ensure consistency. Before cutover, Option C (correct) plans a detailed cutover window that explicitly includes a tested rollback procedure, which is crucial for mitigating risks. Finally, Option D (correct) executes the cutover and performs final validation. An incorrect order, particularly skipping validation or rollback planning, would embody the anti-pattern of attempting online migration without a fallback plan.

text: A company wants to modernize a legacy monolithic Java application by containerizing it and deploying it to Amazon ECS. The application has several dependencies and a complex build process. The solutions architect needs to define a clear sequence of steps to successfully containerize the application and prepare it for deployment to AWS. Order the following steps for containerizing a legacy application for migration to Amazon ECS.
options: ["Analyze the application's runtime environment, dependencies, and external configurations to identify containerization requirements.","Build a Docker image for the application, ensuring all dependencies are included and the application starts correctly.","Create a Dockerfile that defines the application's environment, dependencies, and startup commands.","Test the Docker image locally to ensure the application functions as expected within the container before deploying to Amazon ECS."]
explanation: The first step in containerization is understanding the application. Option A (correct) involves analyzing the application's environment and dependencies. Based on this analysis, Option C (correct) creates a Dockerfile, which is the blueprint for the container image. With the Dockerfile, Option B (correct) builds the Docker image. Finally, Option D (correct) tests the Docker image locally to validate its functionality before pushing it to a registry or deploying it to ECS. Incorrect ordering would lead to building images without proper definitions or deploying untested containers.

text: A small business needs to migrate an on-premises SQL Server database to Amazon RDS for SQL Server. The database is not excessively large, and a simple, one-time migration method is preferred to minimize complexity. The solutions architect has decided to use the native SQL Server backup and restore functionality, leveraging Amazon S3 as an intermediate storage. Order the following steps for migrating a SQL Server database to Amazon RDS for SQL Server using native backup/restore.
options: ["Generate a full backup of the on-premises SQL Server database.","Create an Amazon S3 bucket in the same AWS Region as the target Amazon RDS instance.","Upload the SQL Server backup file from on-premises to the created Amazon S3 bucket.","Restore the database backup from Amazon S3 to the Amazon RDS for SQL Server instance and configure application connectivity."]
explanation: The migration process begins by preparing the target environment for the backup file. Option B (correct) creates an Amazon S3 bucket, which will serve as the temporary storage for the backup. Next, Option A (correct) generates a full backup of the on-premises database. Once the backup is created, Option C (correct) uploads the backup file to the S3 bucket. Finally, Option D (correct) restores the database from S3 to the Amazon RDS instance and configures application connectivity. Incorrect ordering would mean the S3 bucket isn't ready or the backup isn't available for restoration.

text: A company plans to rehost several on-premises Windows servers to AWS using AWS Application Migration Service (MGN). Order the typical steps for performing a rehost migration with MGN.
options: ["Install the AWS Replication Agent on the source servers.","Configure replication settings and launch test instances.","Perform a cutover to the newly launched AWS instances.","Monitor data replication and ensure synchronization."]
explanation: The process begins by installing the AWS Replication Agent (Option A) on the source servers to enable data replication. After installation, monitoring data replication (Option D) ensures data is continuously synchronized. Next, replication settings are configured, and test instances are launched (Option B) to validate the migrated servers. Finally, a cutover (Option C) is performed to switch production traffic to the AWS instances.

text: A development team needs to convert an on-premises Oracle database schema to PostgreSQL for migration to Amazon RDS. Order the typical steps for using AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT).
options: ["Connect AWS SCT to the source Oracle database and the target PostgreSQL database.","Analyze the source schema for compatibility issues and conversion complexity.","Apply the converted schema to the target PostgreSQL database.","Convert the schema objects from Oracle to PostgreSQL using SCT."]
explanation: The process starts by connecting AWS SCT to both the source and target databases (Option A). After connection, SCT analyzes the source schema (Option B) to identify any conversion challenges. Next, SCT is used to convert the schema objects (Option D) from the source to the target format. Finally, the converted schema is applied (Option C) to the target PostgreSQL database.

text: A company needs to migrate petabytes of archival data from an on-premises data center to Amazon S3, but network bandwidth is limited. Order the steps for using AWS Snowball Edge for offline data migration.
options: ["Connect the Snowball Edge device to the on-premises network.","Ship the Snowball Edge device back to AWS.","Request an AWS Snowball Edge device from the AWS Management Console.","Transfer the data from on-premises storage to the Snowball Edge device."]
explanation: The process begins by requesting an AWS Snowball Edge device (Option C) through the AWS Management Console.
